pending_selection.hook_sentence: Two people edited the same song. This works out what each of them changed, combines both, and plays you the one bar where they actually disagree.
pending_selection.what_it_is: A three-way merge for symbolic music, and underneath it a merge algebra for timelines: given a common ancestor and two edited versions, derive each side's edits in musical terms, produce a merged result, and flag only genuine collisions. Text and XML merges fail here because they reconcile tags rather than time.
pending_selection.behaviour_descriptor: see and hear it | two edited files plus their ancestor | interactive visual + audio | music and version control
closest_prior_art_found: musicdiff (github.com/gregchapman-dev/musicdiff) - diff and visualisation of two scores for OMR evaluation; inspected directly, no merge by design
'A diff procedure for music score files', DLfM 2019 - research diff
Mongeau-Sankoff melodic edit distance and polyphonic alignment work - similarity measure, not an edit script or merge
GitDaw - converts Ableton .als to JSON for git text merge; no model of musical time
CRDT collaborative score editors - real-time convergence, not ancestor-based asynchronous merge
proposed_milestones: M1 vertical slice: dependency-free MIDI reader, timed-event model, merge of note add/delete/velocity with unchanged timing, one HTML page with piano rolls and playback
M2 time interaction: edits that insert or remove musical time and move later material; overlapping-region conflicts, rendered and auditionable A/B
M3 alignment without a trustworthy ancestor: recognise moved or transposed sections as moved; flagged as the rung most likely to fail
M4 real files: multiple tracks, tempo maps, controller curves, round-trip preservation of bytes not understood
M5 second binding: same core against subtitles or an edit decision list, as evidence the primitive generalises; git merge driver as a thin adapter
M6 evidence pack: property tests, exhaustive small-case verification, fuzzing against an oracle, and controls (disjoint edits never conflict, identical edits never conflict, re-runs byte-identical)

write the MIDI parser here rather than take a dependency (likely yes)
